Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a couple ask/next steps on the procurement side so we can line up an onboarding timeline: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Pilot scope: 50k tokens/day steady state for API-based inference + 10k embedding units for search tests.
- Security: SOC2 in progress (expected Q4), offer for an on-demand security review with our team.
- Commercial: pricing model is usage-based; pilot discount proposed in SOW draft attached.

Procurement readiness questions (can you confirm?):
1) Preferred payment method: Purchase Order (PO) vs. corporate card?
2) Typical vendor onboarding lead time at Asterion? Any mandatory forms (W-9, vendor packet, security questionnaire)?
3) Is there interest in going through a cloud marketplace (AWS Marketplace / Azure) to speed procurement?

Attached: Redwood_SOW_draft_v2.pdf — draft SOW & proposed pilot pricing. I also attached a short AP routing checklist (I'll share separately if useful).

If PO is required, we'll need the procurement contact and any vendor registration portal link so our finance team can submit docs. If a card is possible for the pilot, we can typically start within ~7 business days.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync with your procurement or ProcureOps contact early next week to align paperwork and timeline. What works on your side?

Thanks, Karthik — useful summary. A few quick answers and context from procurement: 

- Payment method: Asterion generally pays vendors via PO and ACH for anything over $10k/month. For short pilots, Procurement will sometimes approve virtual card payments but that requires vendor registration and our payments team sign-off.
- Mandatory docs: W-9, vendor profile (submitted through our vendor portal), and our standard data handling addendum for cloud vendors. Security questionnaire is required for production, pilot can proceed with an NDA + network isolation agreement.
- Lead time: vendor onboarding currently averaging 30–45 calendar days once we have all docs (tax forms, bank info, and vendor portal registration).

We are interested in a marketplace route if Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace — Procurement prefers that for recurring SaaS because billing is simpler. If not, PO/ACH is our default.

I'll loop in Jacob from ProcureOps to share the vendor portal link and the procurement packet. Can you please confirm whether Redwood accepts virtual card payments and share a completed W-9? Also — are you able to provide a short SOW + invoice for the pilot (so the finance team has a line item to route through the portal)?

Best,
Sophie Lang
Head of Vendor Operations
Asterion Therapeutics
Sophie.Lang@asteriontx.com

Hi all — I’m Jacob from ProcureOps. Quick notes and what we need to move forward: 

1) Vendor portal: register here — https://vendor.asteriontx.com/register — required fields: legal name, tax ID, bank ACH (optional if paying by card), remit address, primary contact.
2) Docs: we need a completed W-9, signed SOW, and insurance certificate (general liability) listed on the vendor packet. If Redwood has an external security attestation PDF (even a readiness note), attach that to the portal — it speeds the review.
3) Timeline: once portal registration and docs are submitted, standard review is ~30 business days but we often expedite pilot vendors in 7–10 business days if we get a virtual card or a PO with expedited approval.
4) Virtual card option: we can issue a single-use virtual card for the pilot invoice if Redwood accepts card payment and can process virtual card numbers. Please confirm the billing contact to receive the card details.

Action items for Redwood (to ProcureOps inbox):
- Upload W-9 and SOW to vendor portal.
- Provide insurance certificate or confirmation of policy limits.
- Indicate whether you accept virtual card payments (yes confirmed by Ben in CC).

Jacob O'Neil
